note: The document gives only general data-protection law items for this country, with no stated AI-harm rule or authority.

facts.fact: Communication Technologies Minister Sofien Hemissi said his ministry has begun drafting legal and regulatory frameworks for responsible use of AI, protecting data and privacy.
facts.system: legal and regulatory frameworks for responsible AI use

facts.fact: The Rights and Freedoms Committee reviewed a 123-article draft organic law on personal data protection that, per its chairman, regulates the use of artificial intelligence and establishes the right not to be subject to a solely automated decision, with impact assessments for high-risk processing.
facts.system: Draft organic law on personal data protection

facts.fact: A signed opinion column in L'Economiste Maghrebin says Tunisia has no text specifically governing the use of AI in the public sphere and no interministerial AI governance body.

The Rights and Liberties Committee's minutes of 17 February 2026 record sponsors presenting a 132-article organic-law proposal on personal data that regulates the use of AI, gives a right not to be subject to a solely automated decision and requires impact assessment for high-risk processing; the committee decided to continue examining it.

facts.fact: Lawyer Zied El Air says organic bill No. 095/2025, tabled in July 2025 by seventeen members of parliament, contains provisions dedicated to artificial intelligence and an independent supervisory authority with sanctioning powers, and is still in committee.
